title: Zero-/Few-Shot Anomaly Classification for Transistor Using Multimodal CLIP Retrieval Augmented
abstract: Detecting anomalies in transistors is a challenging task due to the intricate features distinguishing normal from abnormal components. This paper introduces a zero-shot and few-shot anomaly classification framework for transistors using a retrieval-augmented multimodal approach. We focus on two critical parts of the transistor: the Component BOX and the Metal Legs. Utilizing Florence2 for prompt-based bounding box generation and Segment Anything Model2 (SAM2) for segmentation, we create precise masks for each part. Embeddings generated through Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) are employed to classify each component effectively. For the few-shot learning scenario, we implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to simulate learning from both images and textual data, enhancing the anomaly classification performance. Our zero-shot model achieved an fl score of 70.5, while the few-shot model attained an improved fl score of 77.0, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach in transistor anomaly detection.

title: A Survey on RAG-Based Multimodal Embedding Techniques
abstract: In real-world applications, knowledge often exists in multimodal forms, which traditional text-only Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques struggle to handle effectively. To overcome this limitation, recent research has focused on integrating multimodal embedding techniques into RAG systems, enabling models to process diverse data types and improve generation accuracy. This survey provides a comprehensive review of RAG techniques augmented with multimodal embeddings, covering the underlying architecture, key developments, evaluation methodologies, and practical applications. We categorize existing works from multiple perspectives, including their embedding strategies and cross-modal integration mechanisms, and highlight key findings and performance improvements across tasks. In particular, we find that multimodal RAG systems achieve significant gains in tasks like medical image analysis and cross-modal content generation by grounding outputs in relevant retrieved information. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline future directions for this emerging field.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Embodied Agents
abstract: Embodied agents operating in complex and uncertain environments face considerable challenges. While some advanced agents handle complex manipulation tasks with proficiency, their success often hinges on extensive training data to develop their capabilities. In contrast, humans typically rely on recalling past experiences and analogous situations to solve new problems. Aiming to emulate this human approach in robotics, we introduce the Retrieval-Augmented Embodied Agent (RAEA). This innovative system equips robots with a form of shared memory, significantly enhancing their performance. Our approach integrates a policy retriever, allowing robots to access relevant strategies from an external policy memory bank based on multi-modal inputs. Additionally, a policy generator is employed to assimilate these strategies into the learning process, enabling robots to formulate effective responses to tasks. Extensive testing of RAEA in both simulated and real-world scenarios demonstrates its superior performance over traditional methods, representing a major leap forward in robotic technology.

title: Rationale-Guided Retrieval: Fusing Multimodal Chain-of-Thought and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Grounded Reasoning
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated significant capabilities in processing and interpreting complex, real-world information that spans text, images, audio, and video. However, they often struggle with tasks requiring deep, verifiable reasoning, particularly when external knowledge is needed. Existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Systems can fetch relevant information but lack a sophisticated mechanism to synthesize it through a transparent reasoning process. Concurrently, Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (MCoT) Methods generate reasoning steps but often hallucinate information not present in the provided context. This paper introduces a novel architecture that synergistically integrates these two paradigms. Our system employs a dynamic, rationale-guided retrieval process where the intermediate reasoning steps generated by an MCoT module actively refine subsequent queries for the RAG component. This iterative loop between reasoning and retrieval allows the model to dynamically seek and ground its thought process in high-precision, contextually relevant information. Our experimental results on the ScienceQA and A-OKVQA benchmarks show that this architecture significantly outperforms traditional unimodal and multimodal models in both accuracy and the faithfulness of its generated explanations.

title: Adaptive Multimodal Fusion Architecture for Heterogeneous Embedding Spaces in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation systems integrate external information to mitigate hallucinations in large language models, yet existing multimodal retrieval-augmented generation implementations struggle with heterogeneous embedding spaces from diverse sources. This study introduces an adaptive multimodal fusion architecture that addresses the critical challenge of integrating embeddings from research models and commercial application programming interfaces with varying dimensionalities (ranging from 768 to 1,536 dimensions) and training paradigms. We propose a source-agnostic framework comprising lightweight adapters, cross-modal attention mechanisms, and learned confidence calibration. The system was evaluated on 20,000 multimodal samples across image, video, audio, and text modalities, demonstrating significant performance improvements. The architecture enables end-to-end training without separate pretraining steps while maintaining flexibility for pretrained encoders. Experimental results show 7.2% improvement in Recall@10 compared to single-best source approaches (82.4% versus 89.6%), with expected calibration error of 0.048, indicating well-calibrated confidence scores. The framework achieves graceful degradation with only 3.8% performance reduction when one modality becomes unavailable and maintains 81.3% of in-domain performance in zero-shot domain transfer tasks. This work advances multimodal retrieval-augmented generation systems by enabling plug-and-play integration of heterogeneous embedding sources while preserving computational efficiency and interpretability.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Egocentric Video Captioning
abstract: Understanding human actions from videos offirst-person view poses significant challenges. Most prior approaches explore representation learning on egocentric videos only, while overlooking the potential benefit of exploiting existing large-scale third-person videos. In this paper, (1) we develop EgoInstructor, a retrieval-augmented multimodal captioning model that automatically retrieves semantically relevant third-person instructional videos to enhance the video captioning of egocentric videos, (2) for training the cross-view retrieval module, we devise an au-tomatic pipeline to discover ego-exo video pairs from distinct large-scale egocentric and exocentric datasets, (3) we train the cross-view retrieval module with a novel EgoEx-oNCE loss that pulls egocentric and exocentric video features closer, by aligning them to shared text features that describe similar actions, (4) through extensive experiments, our cross-view retrieval module demonstrates superior performance across seven benchmarks. Regarding egocen-tric video captioning, EgoInstructor exhibits significant improvements by leveraging third-person videos as references.

title: Private Metadata-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Reconstruction for Missing Modalities in Multimodal Federated Learning
abstract: Multimodal federated learning (MFL) enables clients with distributed multimodal data to collaboratively train models while preserving privacy, and has been widely used in multi-domain IoT and blockchain-enabled applications where clients collect heterogeneous data such as images, text, and sensor signals. A key challenge is missing modalities, i.e., only some samples have all modalities (i.e., aligned) while many samples lack one or more modalities. Existing reconstruction-based methods usually rely on scarce aligned samples or dispersed global semantic cues, but data heterogeneity and privacy constraints make such global cues difficult to retrieve and exploit effectively. We proposePRAR, which decouples learning into metadata prototype retrieval and prototype-augmented reconstruction. For retrieval, each client summarizes local missing-modality embeddings into compact metadata prototypes and perturbs them via the Gaussian mechanism. The noisy prototypes form a differentially private global metadata prototype pool, whose metadata records support access control and semantic top-$K$retrieval. For reconstruction, we train a prototype-augmented reconstructor that combines aligned supervision with retrieved metadata prototypes through a residual structure. We provide privacy and utility guarantees for retrieval, and show that the residual design minimizes the mean squared error (MSE) for missing-modality reconstruction. Experiments on four multimodal datasets against five strong baselines show thatPRARimproves cross-modal retrieval and multimodal classification by an average of 4.77% and 6.07% over the strongest baseline.

title: Multimodal RAG for Enhanced Information Retrieval and Generation in Retail
abstract: This study explores the use of Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models to enhance information retrieval and generation in retail applications. By combining both structured (e.g., sales data, inventory levels) and unstructured (e.g., product descriptions, customer reviews, images) data sources, RAG models improve the generation of accurate and contextually relevant content. The study evaluates the model's performance on a large-scale retail dataset consisting of product sales data, customer interaction logs, and multimedia content across multiple retail channels. Performance is compared to traditional retrieval methods in terms of accuracy, response quality, computational efficiency, and real-world business impact. Results demonstrate significant improvements in recommendation accuracy 92% and customer engagement metrics. This research contributes to the evolving field of multimodal AI, demonstrating the advantages of hybrid approaches in dynamic business environments and providing practical implementation guidelines for retail organizations.

title: Enhancing Automated Interview Performance Evaluation Using Multimodal Emotion Detection and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Conventional interview assessment is based on human perception, tending towards subjectivity, variability, and inefficiencies, particularly when evaluating large groups of candidates. To overcome these drawbacks, we introduce an AI-based automated interview assessment platform that combines multimodal emotion recognition with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to deliver objective, data-driven analysis. Our method evaluates verbal (text-based answers), non-verbal (facial reactions, gaze, and body language), and paralinguistic (speech tone, pitch, and clarity) signals to provide a complete assessment of interview performance. By utilizing GPT-3.5 with LLaMA Index, the model reads and places key findings from interview transcripts into context to provide comprehensive and explainable feedback. Moreover, OpenFace and Wav2Vec are utilized for face expression and speech emotion recognition that are combined utilizing a hybrid multimodal approach in order to do a strong assessment. The assessment is done via a Total Score metric, examining candidates on understanding content (30%), confidence, and fluency (20%), emotional control (20%), non-verbal communication (15%), and paralinguistic features (15%). Experimental validation on the MIT Interview Dataset shows that the system proposed here enhances assessment accuracy, fairness, and consistency, outperforming human evaluators in delivering standardized reviews. Such discoveries show the promise of multimodal AI-driven evaluations for automated recruitment, talent assessment, and educational uses, opening the way for scalable, bias-free interview reviews)

title: Application of Retrieval-Augmented Generation in video
abstract: The application of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology in the field of text has become increasingly mature. This paper innovatively proposes a new method for applying RAG technology to video retrieval. The method abandons the traditional retrieval method based on video frame descriptions, which often tends to break the context of the video. This paper proposes a context-aware dynamic fragmenting strategy that can intelligently adjust the fragmenting threshold according to the complexity and amount of information in the video content. In addition, to maximize the preservation of video information and by utilizing QKD (Quantum Key Distribution) quantum encryption technology, this method also performs multimodal feature extraction on video fragments, including audio, visual, and text dimensions, ensuring that the loss of information is minimized and data security.

title: Enhancing Learning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: This survey paper investigates the role of Retrieval Augmented Generation models in improving student learning by effectively capturing and describing video content. The RAG model leverages multimodal data by combining text, visual, and audio data to generate question-based content. By analyzing video content based on speech and visual metadata, the model can capture and record important content in videos, saving teachers and students time in entering important information. This approach refines the content of the video, making it easier to extract important details and useful insights. Integrating AI-driven RAG models into learning models opens up new possibilities for personalized learning. Students receive AI-generated content that is accurate and tailored to their learning needs, focusing on the most important aspects of the video lessons. This technique not only makes the video easier to use, but also keeps students engaged by creating questions that encourage deeper understanding of the material. The results of this research demonstrate the potential of the RAG model to transform the learning process by increasing the retrieval of important information and improving access to important content. The integration of various devices into this AI-based approach represents a significant advance in learning by enabling interactive and effective learning.

title: GenAI-Powered Clinical Libraries: Enhancing Patient-Centric Care with Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multimodal Search
abstract: Healthcare organizations are now producing enormous volumes of unstructured data in many forms—clinical guidelines, PDFs, presentations, and even diagnostic images. Existing clinical libraries largely depend on keyword-based search, which often yields long, unfocused lists that clinicians must sift through before finding relevant information. This work introduces a Clinical Library powered by generative AI. The system combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [1], multimodal content ingestion, and large language models (LLMs) to create a more intuitive search experience. Instead of wading through document lists, clinicians can ask natural-language questions and receive concise, multilingual answers backed by citations. Safeguards against hallucinations are built in, ensuring that outputs remain evidence-based and trustworthy for clinical practice.

title: Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Reasoning for Internet of Things: A Retrieval-Augmented Large Language and Vision Assistant Framework
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) generates massive multimodal data that can potentially power sophisticated analytics using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and give rise to new paradigms where users interact with IoT systems through natural language prompts and query IoT applications for complex insights. However, these models pose significant privacy risks when sensitive data, such as personal identifiers or proprietary information, is shared for model training or finetuning at scale. In this paper, we propose a novel privacy-enhanced Visual Question Answering (VQA) framework tailored for IoT scenarios. Unlike prior VQA pipelines that omit explicit privacy controls or rely on coarse box masking, our framework applies semantic segmentation and labeling to isolate sensitive content, which is removed or obfuscated via diffusion inpainting before model processing. Our framework applies semantic segmentation and labeling to isolate sensitive content, which is removed or obfuscated via diffusion inpainting before model processing. We then leverage parameter-efficient Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to finetune a language–vision assistant and incorporate Ghost Clipping to reduce gradient-based data leakage. For questions that require context beyond the processed IoT images, we introduce Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to draw upon external knowledge sources and deliver insights. Experimental results on a customized IoT-oriented subset of the OK-VQA dataset constructed via a CLIP similarity score to an IoT phrase bank and a light COCO super-category filter illustrate that our framework preserves privacy while achieving competitive accuracy, even outperforming standard non-private baselines. Protecting privacy at both the data preprocessing and finetuning stages, this work offers a scalable solution that meets the stringent privacy demands of real-world IoT environments. On the OK-VQA, which contains 14,055 images and QA pairs, our framework attains 76.1% accuracy without privacy consideration, and 49.3%–75.2% for a privacy budget ranging from 0.5 to 5, even surpassing a non-private LLaVA-7B baseline (73.7%).

title: ExplainHM++: Explainable Harmful Meme Detection With Retrieval-Augmented Debate Between Large Multimodal Models
abstract: Identifying harmful memes is challenging due to their implicit meanings, which are not always evident from texts and images alone. Existing solutions often lack clear explanations to justify their decisions. To address this gap, we propose an explainable approach,ExplainHM++, which detects harmful memes by reasoning over competing rationales from both harmful and harmless perspectives. First, inspired by the capabilities of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in text generation and multimodal reasoning, we developExplainHM, a one-stage multimodal debate in which LMMs generate explanations through contradictory arguments. Second, we fine-tune a small language model to serve as a judge in the debate, improving the integration of harmfulness rationales with the multimodal content of memes. However, we observe that a naive multimodal debate remains vulnerable, as it heavily depends on the inherent reasoning ability of LMMs to understand the memes. Given the evolving and noisy nature of memes, we further introduce a meme sample retrieval mechanism and a retrieval-augmented debate paradigm to strengthen and refine LMM-generated explanations. Extensive experiments on three public meme datasets demonstrate thatExplainHM++not only outperforms state-of-the-art methods but also provides superior, interpretable explanations for harmful meme detection.

title: Multi-Passage Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Generation Model for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
abstract: Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering is a challenging task that requires a VQA system to utilize external knowledge to answer questions about a given image. Most current retrieval-augmented methods suffer from two notable limitations. Firstly, these methods tend to convert images into plain text and subsequently discard the original image input, resulting in a loss of valuable visual information. Secondly, they often fail to utilize multiple retrieved passages effectively, typically depending on just one passage to generate answers or directly concatenating multiple passages, which leads to excessively long sequences of knowledge input. To overcome the limitations of previous methods, we introduce an innovative retriever-generator framework for knowledge-based VQA. This framework comprises a Multimodal Queries-oriented Knowledge Retriever (MQ-KR) and a Multi-Passage Retrieval-Augmented Generator (MP-RAG). We utilize the original image directly for both knowledge retrieval and answer generation. The generator is a multimodal language generation model capable of producing accurate answers by effectively aggregating evidence from multiple passages. Our proposed method achieves a VQA Score of 59.89% on the OK-VQA dataset, surpassing the SOTA retrieval-augmented method by a large margin (+4.37%).

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with GPT-4o-mini: Integrating Configurable Chunking, Hybrid Search, and Multimodal Image Retrieval
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems significantly enhance the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) by grounding responses in external knowledge. We implemented a RAG system utilizing the GPT-4o-mini model to advance knowledge base management, configurable document processing, and multimodal information retrieval. We constructed a modular knowledge base framework that supports creation, configuration, and granular management of diverse information sources, including text in formats of TXT, PDF, CSV, and extracted visual data. The key feature of the developed framework is the user-configurable document chunking process, allowing optimization of text segmentation through adjustable parameters (chunk size, overlap, custom separators) before ingestion. The framework employs ChromaDB as its vector store, implementing a hybrid search that combines dense vector-based semantic similarity with traditional keyword matching, offering configurable weighting and relevance thresholds. Furthermore, we introduce automated image extraction from PDF documents into knowledge ingestion. Extracted images are indexed with associated metadata and rudimentary captions. In the query process, relevant images are retrieved alongside pertinent text chunks, providing richer, multimodal context to the GPT-4o-mini model. The developed framework highlights the design and implementation details of the components, demonstrating a flexible and efficient construction of RAG systems capable of leveraging both textual and visual information from managed knowledge bases.

title: Multimodal RAG AI for Antenna Geometry Reconstruction from Scientific Literature
abstract: This paper introduces a Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) framework that autonomously reconstructs antenna geometries from scientific literature. Most of the scientific knowledge about antenna design is stored in unstructured documents, where important geometric information is spread out across figures, captions, and descriptive text. The proposed pipeline takes figures and contextual text from PDF files, uses vision-language models to make unified multimodal embeddings, and then stores them in a vector database for semantic retrieval. A retrieval-augmented reasoning pipeline processes retrieved multimodal evidence to find antenna structures, uses Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to extract dimensional annotations, and uses computer vision techniques like Stable Diffusion Inpainting to isolate clean geometric contours. The reconstructed geometries are turned into vectors and saved as Drawing Exchange Format (DXF) files that can be used in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) programs for electromagnetic simulations. The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of transforming unstructured antenna literature into structured, simulation-ready geometric representations by integrating multimodal retrieval, vision–language reasoning, and computer vision techniques. Hence, the design time to verify an antenna design from scientific literature is minimized due to the proposed pipeline.

title: LLM-Therapist: A RAG-Based Multimodal Behavioral Therapist as Healthcare Assistant
abstract: Systems and services based on Large Language Models (LLM) are trending in the applied field of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The emergence of GPTs and subsequent improvements such as, unsupervised pre-training and transformer architecture have lead to its ability to generate human-quality text and understand context effectively. This has opened huge opportunity in healthcare domain to use AI-based assistant systems that can offer tailored recommendations and guidance for patients in numerous scenarios by considering multimodal data. This paper proposes LLM-Therapist as a multimodal personalized health care assistant for various types of patients. title: COME: Towards Superior Embeddings for Multimodal RAG with Heterogeneous Input
abstract: Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation (MRAG) is crucial for real-world applications that involve interwoven text and image content. However, current approaches primarily concentrate on interpreting multimodal documents while neglecting the understanding of multimodal queries. Addressing this gap presents two major challenges: 1) there is a significant shortage of high-quality, real-world data for multimodal query retrieval within the MRAG domain; 2) previous methods encounter modeling difficulties due to the heterogeneous nature of input data. To tackle these challenges, we propose COME, a Curriculum-Optimized Multimodal Embedding framework multimodal RAG with heterogeneous input. COME employs a three-stage curriculum learning paradigm to build model capabilities progressively, moving from easier to more challenging tasks, and to benefit from various types of data. Additionally, to further improve discriminative alignment for heterogeneous inputs, we incorporate an adaptive margin loss that dynamically adjusts semantic distances based on task requirements, thus mitigating the issue of heterogeneous input across different tasks. To finetune and verify the model, we also construct a dataset featuring heterogeneous inputs, sourced from real-world industrial RAG application scenarios. Extensive experiments on document retrieval benchmarks demonstrate that COME achieves superior performance.

title: Evaluating RAG Pipeline in Multimodal LLM-based Question Answering Systems
abstract: Recent improvements have increased the adoption of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) over traditional uni-modal systems since they can manage and combine information from several types of data. However, current multimodal systems have certain limitations, particularly when it comes to retrieving relevant information for domain-specific queries. This study investigates how Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approaches can help multimodal LLMs provide more contextually accurate answers from external data sources for Question and Answering (Q&A) systems. The research compares two state-of-the-art models—Google's Gemini-1.0-Pro and OpenAI's GPT-4o-mini for a Q&A system that utilizes Multimodal RAG architecture. Additionally, the study incorporates several embedding models, including Text-embedding-ada-002-v2 and embedding-001, to further improve retrieval performance. In the absence of any standardized criterion, the study used a custom-made multimodal dataset and evaluated the system using six metrics defined by human analysis. The results revealed that using RAG with multimodal LLMs greatly improves performance in Q&A tasks, with GPT-4o-mini slightly outperforming Gemini-1.0-Pro by 5%. These findings promote advancements for research in the field of Multimodal-RAG systems and highlight their potential for much better information retrieval in specialized areas.

title: EduRAG: A Multimodal Explainable RAG System With Deterministic Token Grounding
abstract: LLMs (Large Language Models) offer quick access to information, but they tend to be unreliable when used for academic purposes. Because of this, they often generate factually incorrect information (known as factual hallucinations) and do not often provide reliable citations. In this work, we introduce EduRAG, a multimodal, explainable retrieval-augmented generation model, specifically engineered to build trust in the field of education. It includes a hybrid information retrieval system incorporating the advantages of the BM25 lexical match, combined with FAISS vector space embeddings, and fine-tuned via Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE) query expansion and cross-encoder re-ranking on MS-MARCO as a superior alternative to other methods. To address the constraints arising from the high computational cost associated with conventional attribution methods, such as SHAP values, we introduce a multi-level attribution framework that enables the transparent inspection of evidence on the chunk level with cross-encoder evidence scores, deterministic token-level grounding heatmaps for hallucination detection, and source disagreement for contradiction spotting between different retrieved sources. Controlled experimental results conducted with a customized dataset consisting of 97 educational queries demonstrate that EduRAG achieves a Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) score of 0.7784 and Recall@5 score of 0.8763. A targeted visual evaluation on 15 diagram-specific queries demonstrates visual MRR of 0.967 and Recall@5 of 100%, validating VLM-enabled multimodal retrieval. The answers generated by the model yield a BERTScore F1 of 0.8952, faithfulness score of 0.8924, a 94% citation validity rate with verifiable provenance, and 85.5% token grounding accuracy. The impact of each component in the proposed system is validated via an ablation study involving three retrieval-based models.

title: Multimodal Clinical Decision Support for Melanoma Diagnosis Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Vision-Language Models
abstract: Malignant melanoma is a lethal form of skin cancer, where early and precise diagnosis is essential for improving survival. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promise in dermoscopic image analysis, they often neglect patient metadata that clinicians routinely consider. Vision-language models (VLMs) provide a unified architecture for multimodal understanding; however, their utility in clinical domains remains limited due to domain mismatch and lack of adaptation. To address these limitations, we propose a retrieval-augmented framework that integrates pre-trained VLMs with a multimodal vector database of dermoscopic images and patient metadata. For each input, the system retrieves semantically similar cases and inserts them into structured prompts, which enable few-shot classification without fine-tuning. Our method outperforms image-based, text-based, and embedding-fusion baselines by yielding higher F1-scores and reducing both false positives and false negatives. Our findings support retrieval-augmented prompting as a reliable and scalable approach to clinical decision support in melanoma diagnosis.

title: A Hierarchical Retrieval-Augmented Generative Intelligence Framework for Multimodal Clinical Data Interpretation and Medical Report Automation
abstract: In developing countries, outpatient clinics can be characterized by congestion because of patients who did not receive test results but would like clarifications, especially of longterm patients or pregnant patients. The difficulty of conventional medical documentation prevents the understanding of it by nonmedical staff, requiring one to visit a hospital multiple times to ask a specific question.This study introduces a sophisticated AI architecture called Hierarchical Retrieval-Augmented Generative Intelligence (HRAGI) that is capable of interpreting medical records and present findings to a patient based on various data points. It skillfully manipulates different sources of inputsCT images, ultrasound images and lab reports- by applying special AI models to identify relevant medical data. The presence of a rules-based mechanism that classifies patients into risk categories, with the normal, mild, moderate, and critical respectively, following the accepted medical guidelines. The hierarchical structure of the system retrieves data in a progressive manner, firstly assembling the clinical context, secondly refining it with evidence based guidelines and finally producing summaries that are understandable. All the outputs have to be reviewed and approved by the physicians before they are disseminated to the patients to ensure safety. Compared to the conventional clinic protocol, or the primitive artificial intelligence, this approach reduces the number of unnecessary hospital visits, saves time of physicians and allows making the process of patient-centered decision-making faster .

title: Oil-Immersed Transformer Diagnosis Based on On-Device Large Model with Multimodal Sensing and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Power transformer failures can cause severe grid disruptions, yet traditional diagnostic methods such as dissolved gas analysis(DGA), infrared thermography, and acoustic sensing each capture only partial fault information, resulting in inconsistent and delayed assessments. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Diagnosis(MMRAGDiag), an on-device transformer fault diagnosis framework that integrates DGA, infrared thermal imaging, acoustic sensing, and manual inspection text through a retrieval-augmented large language model. The system fuses heterogeneous sensor outputs into structured prompts, retrieves relevant maintenance knowledge from a local database, and generates both diagnostic conclusions and maintenance plans in natural language. Implemented entirely on a portable inspection terminal, MM-RAGDiag enables real-time, knowledge-grounded fault detection without cloud connectivity, suitable for bandwidth-limited substations. A proprietary dataset of$\mathbf{1, 0 0 0}$oil-immersed transformer inspections was constructed to evaluate the framework. Experimental results demonstrate that MM-RAGDiag achieves 97.1 % diagnostic accuracy and a Bilingual Evaluation Understudy-4 score of 72.4, surpassing all unimodal baselines. The ablation and human-Artificial Intelligence comparison studies further confirm that multimodal fusion and retrieval augmentation significantly enhance diagnostic reliability and interpretability, approaching expert-level performance in real-world inspections.

title: Empowering Access to Public Services: An Analysis on Multimodal, Retrieval-Augmented Chatbots for Indic Language Support to Farmers
abstract: Rural communities in India face persistent barri-ers-linguistic diversity, low digital and language literacy, and limited domain-specific resources-when accessing government welfare information. This survey reviews advances in generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation, and multimodal chatbot systems for low-resource Indic languages, centered on the development of a remote-accessible assistant supporting voice, text, and image queries. We examine methods for unifying multimodal inputs, improving machine translation and information retrieval in chat-based frameworks, and grounding responses in official policy content. Key challenges include dialectal variation, data scarcity, and cost-efficient deployment at scale. By synthesizing current research and identifying gaps, this work provides design directions for robust, inclusive AI chatbots that bridge information accessibility gaps in rural India.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey of Security Challenges and Countermeasures
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance the accuracy and reliability of generated content by integrating retrieval and generation modules. However, their multi-module architecture introduces complex security risks. For instance, the PoisonedRAG attack demonstrates how injecting a small number of malicious texts into the knowledge base can manipulate the system to generate specific outputs. This paper provides the first comprehensive analysis of RAG security threats from a full-chain perspective, including adversarial attacks, data poisoning, privacy leaks, and a novel trigger-based backdoor poisoning attack. We also review existing defense techniques, such as robustness enhancement and privacy protection frameworks, and explore future research directions like dynamic defense, multi-modal threat handling, and trigger-specific countermeasures, offering insights for building secure and trustworthy RAG applications.

title: Multimodal Quiz Generation via RAG with LLM-as-Judge Evaluation
abstract: This paper presents a novel multimodal quiz generation framework that integrates audio, visual, and textual data using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. The system leverages LLaVA for vision-language understanding and LLaMA 3.1 for text generation to produce contextually relevant and pedagogically meaningful multiple-choice questions (MCQs) from lecture videos. This approach addresses key limitations of traditional text-only quiz generation models by capturing richer, multimodal information. The system was tested on a real-world use case, generating 15 MCQs from the first lecture in an introductory computer science course. To evaluate the effectiveness of the generated quizzes, we designed a two-stage evaluation framework. In the first stage, we assessed retrieval and generation performance using standard metrics such as Hit Rate, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Correctness, Relevance, and Faithfulness. In the second stage, we examined how closely AI evaluations align with human expert judgments. We involved four human raters and three LLM-as-Judge models—Claude 3 Sonnet, GPT-4, and LLaMA 3.1—to evaluate each question. To analyze agreement, we used Percentage Agreement, Cohen's Kappa, Spearman's Rho, and Krippendorff's Alpha, capturing both exact matches and ordinal consistency. Our results show high retrieval accuracy and reasonable alignment between LLM based and human assessments, particularly in factual and procedural questions. However, discrepancies emerged in questions requiring deeper reasoning or visual interpretation, where human raters exhibited stronger consistency. These findings highlight the strengths of LLMs in scalable content generation, while reinforcing the need for human oversight in evaluating complex educational tasks. This work takes a significant step toward more human-aligned and effective AI-driven assessment systems.

title: Multimodal AI for Romanian University Support: An LLM, RAG and Voice Approach
abstract: The era of large language models (LLMs) brings forth a new wave of automation to many fields of activity. In this work we employ the AI advancements catalyzed by these LLMs to create a smart university assistant. A chatbot that comes to assist university enrolled students and staff on administrative, legislative and public interest topics. To this end, we develop a platform that combines Large Language Models, Retrieval Augmented Generation, Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech technologies to automate accessibility to university-related information. We start from openly available models and resources, adapt and finetune them to our target - Romanian question answering with information retrieval - and then release our solutions publicly at https://github.com/Andrei481/RomanianChatbot.

title: ContractIQ : A Multimodal RAG-Based Agentic System for Intelligent Contract Understanding
abstract: When organizations in industries like finance, health-care, real estate, and technology deal with intricate, high-risk contracts, legal contract analysis cannot be avoided. Accurate and proper analysis assists in the interpretation of minute details, evaluation of risks, and adherence in contracts. Smart contractual automation is needed since manual checking is cumbersome and susceptible to errors. By applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), an agentic eleven-coordinated agent, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to interpret legal analysis, the study proposes a legal contract analysis system based on Google's Gemini large language model (LLM). The system includes Clause extraction, definition detection, risk analysis, compliance checks, QnA and summarization. Gemini can be finely adapted to be used in the legal field through LoRA finetuning. Testing achieves strong performance: ROUGE-1 of 0.42, ROUGE-2 of 0.38, ROUGEL of 0.40, F1 score of 0.70, and BLEU of 0.45, indicating high-quality legal text generation. This solution significantly reduces manual labor but with enhanced legal precision and compliance.

title: RAG Beyond Text: Enhancing Image Retrieval in RAG Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for the extraction and retrieval of images in RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) powered Question Answering Conversational Systems that circumvents the limitations of Optical Character Recognition and Large Language Model (OCR-LLM) powered traditional image retrieval approaches. We are leveraging the positional information of images in a vast array of multi-modal (text/image) documents for ingesting image information alongside text, followed by advanced retrieval and prompt engineering techniques to develop an RAG system that maintains the integrity of textual and visual data correlation in responses to queries pertaining to both text and images in QnA solutions and is adept at retrieving both OCR-compatible and OCR-incompatible images. We have successfully incorporated this approach over a variety of multimodal documents ranging from research papers, application documentations, surveys to guides and manuals containing text, images and even tables with images and managed to achieve SoTA (State of The Art) performance over simple to complex queries asked on the mentioned documents. Furthermore, our approach performed explicitly better in cases where Vision Models like GPT-4 Vision fails to accurately retrieve images which are OCR incompatible and pertains to highly customized scientific devices or diagrams and in cases where the image's visual representation is not semantically aligned with textual information but is important to be retrieved for completeness in the response.

title: Structured Multimodal RAG: Document-Aware Retrieval and Alignment for Hallucination Mitigation
abstract: With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs), hallucination remains a persistent challenge, particularly in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems where incomplete or mismatched external contexts may ex-acerbate factual inconsistency issues. This paper proposes a novel multimodal RAG framework that achieves hallucination mitigation through the integration of structured document representation, hybrid retrieval, and feature-enhanced embeddings. First, we construct a multimodal knowledge base that performs structure-aware enhancement on scanned documents and vision-text inputs, maintaining layout and semantic coherence across modalities. Subsequently, we design a hybrid retrieval module combining sparse and dense indexing, with cross-modal relevance ranking mechanisms for reranking. To further improve retrieval quality, we introduce a multimodal feature enhancement layer that enriches embedding representations through vision-text fusion. Comprehensive experiments on multimodal hallucination benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly improves factual consistency, effectively reduces hallucination rates, and achieves superior performance across multiple evaluation metrics.

item.title: Structured Multimodal RAG: Document-Aware Retrieval and Alignment for Hallucination Mitigation
item.abstractNote: With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs), hallucination remains a persistent challenge, particularly in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems where incomplete or mismatched external contexts may ex-acerbate factual inconsistency issues. This paper proposes a novel multimodal RAG framework that achieves hallucination mitigation through the integration of structured document representation, hybrid retrieval, and feature-enhanced embeddings. First, we construct a multimodal knowledge base that performs structure-aware enhancement on scanned documents and vision-text inputs, maintaining layout and semantic coherence across modalities. Subsequently, we design a hybrid retrieval module combining sparse and dense indexing, with cross-modal relevance ranking mechanisms for reranking. To further improve retrieval quality, we introduce a multimodal feature enhancement layer that enriches embedding representations through vision-text fusion. Comprehensive experiments on multimodal hallucination benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly improves factual consistency, effectively reduces hallucination rates, and achieves superior performance across multiple evaluation metrics.

title: Multimodal RAG and Fine-Tuned LLMs for Enhanced Understanding of Electrical Concepts
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into domain-specific digital education requires scalable, multimodal, and semantically rich architectures. This paper presents Electronic Professor, an intelligent avatar framework for electricity education that combines a multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs). The system ingests a heterogeneous corpus of textbooks, circuit diagrams, mathematical formulas, and instructional videos into a FAISS-indexed knowledge base augmented by a GraphRAG knowledge graph. A LangChain and LlamaIndex orchestration layer manages context-aware retrieval, while a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder handles circuit diagram understanding. A prototype using Flan-T5-small demonstrates efficient question answering over 60-plus academic files. Evaluation against BM25 and GPT-4 baselines using BLEU, ROUGE-L, and Precision@K metrics confirms the framework’s advantage in domain-specific retrieval accuracy and generation quality. A student study with 40 undergraduates shows a 72% reduction in average search time and a 43% improvement in interactivity ratings compared to traditional file search. Future work targets LoRA-based fine-tuning of Mistral-7B and Phi-2 to further strengthen multimodal pedagogical reasoning.

title: Semantic Fusion Agent for Multimodal TCM Diagnosis and Cross-Domain RAG Integration
abstract: Recent studies, such as TongueNet and OpenTCM, have explored the application of multi-modal information, including images and text, in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) diagnostics. However, two major challenges remain: (1) the cross-domain acquisition of diverse Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system structures to bridge users' colloquial descriptions with formal medical terminology, and (2) the semantic fusion of these acquired structures to enable precise alignment of multimodal semantics, which is essential in high-stakes domains such as healthcare. To address these challenges, we propose a “Semantic Fusion Agent,” a versatile intermediate component that bridges users' multimodal inputs (e.g., speech, tongue images, and pulse signals) with downstream RAG retrieval systems. This agent understands the structural requirements of target RAG systems across domains and transforms user inputs into structured semantic representations compatible with diverse knowledge base formats. In this way, the agent enhances the transparency of medical terminology by automatically generating accessible explanations, thereby improving user comprehension and trust. It also supports cross-domain semantic translation (e.g., from TCM to Western medicine or psychological diagnostics). The primary contribution of this work is the introduction of a structured semantic fusion mechanism that significantly improves the retrieval precision and structured-generation quality of RAG systems in diagnostic scenarios; we do not claim clinical diagnostic accuracy.

title: Collective Experts Against Noise: Enhancing Social Media Popularity Prediction Via Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Experts
abstract: Social media popularity prediction (SMPP) aims to forecast future engagement of user-generated content and is critical for a wide range of real-world applications. However, existing methods often rely on simple feature fusion or direct use of retrieved neighbors, which can introduce irrelevant signals and overlook cross-modal inconsistencies. To address these limitations, we propose RaMoE, a novel Retrieval-augmented Mixture-of-modal-Experts framework for enhancing SMPP. First, RaMoE employs a field-aware retriever to select historical UGCs that reflect the query’s multimodal context. Second, knowledge-augmented experts align and filter conflicting signals via cross-attention. Finally, a noise-sensitive mixing network adaptively adjusts expert weights to suppress unreliable evidence. Experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that RaMoE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, validating its effectiveness in mitigating retrieval noise and resolving modality conflicts. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/coloreyes/RaMoE.

title: VestiME: A RAG-based Multimodal Fashion Outfit Recommender System
abstract: Fashion plays a significant role in cultures around the world and in the global economy. Similarly to what has happened with other consumer products, the Internet has trans-formed the way people shop for fashion, transitioning from an in-store experience to an increasingly online one thanks to ever-evolving e-commerce. While much of today’s e-commerce experience for fashion still relies on a keyword-search-based approach for web and mobile catalogs, the advent of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) has brought unprecedented opportunities for searching, exploring, and recommending fashion products online. This paper aims to leverage state-of-the-art GenAI and multimodal LLM technologies to provide a different customer experience based on conversational, intent-driven exploration of fashion catalogs and outfit recommendations through our proposed solution, VestiME. The results of our user study involving fashion experts show the potential of these highly interactive, conversational, and multimodal e-commerce experiences for fashion.

title: A Bird Song RAG System Using Multimodal Vector Search
abstract: Understanding and identifying bird species is vital for ecological research, biodiversity conservation, and environmental monitoring. However, bird identification is often difficult for non-experts, especially when relying on partial information such as bird song or species names. To address this, we propose a bird song RAG system using multimodal vector search which is a flexible retrieval system that helps users search for bird species using various types of input sound, key word, and taxonomic knowledge. In this system, Bird song audio, species names (in English and Japanese), and taxonomic data are converted into a vector in a shared multimodal space. In our experiments, taxonomic queries performed best, while bird song retrieval improved significantly through fine-tuning. From our results, careful integration of modalities is crucial, and the system provides both accessible species search and a foundation for future research in biodiversity informatics.

title: Comparative Analysis of Chunking Strategies for Turkish Multimodal RAG Systems
abstract: Geleneksel İçerik Erişimine Dayalı Üretim (RAG) sistemleri; tablo, grafik ve düzensiz yerleşimler içeren karmaşık belgelerle çalışırken bilgi bütünlüğünü korumada genellikle yetersiz kalmaktadır. Bu yapısal sorunların üstesinden gelmek amacıyla bu çalışma, dört farklı parçalama stratejisinin karşılaştırmalı bir analizini sunmaktadır: Basit (Naive), Dinamik, Görsel ve Hibrit RAG. Hibrit mimari; tablo hiyerarşisini koruyan yapıya duyarlı akıllı metin işleme ile hedef odaklı görsel vektör üretimini entegre eden çok aşamalı bir iş akışına dayanmaktadır. Bu stratejilerin performansı; 46 kurumsal entegre rapordan ve 1.380 soru-cevap çiftinden oluşan bir veri seti üzerinde, "LLM-as-a-Judge" yaklaşımı kullanılarak Bağlam Kapsama (Context Recall), Hassasiyet (Precision) ve Doğruluk (Accuracy) metrikleri üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir. Sonuçlar, Hibrit RAG’ın tek modlu sistemlerin sınırlamalarını etkili bir şekilde aştığını göstermektedir. En iyi tek modlu temel yönteme kıyasla Bağlam Kapsama’da 0,82’ye, Hassasiyet’te 0,82’ye ve Cevap Doğruluğu’nda 0,71’e ulaşılmıştır.

title: AI and Machine Learning Powered Impacted Test Case Generation From Multimodal User Stories Using Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Because requirements are constantly changing, modern software systems are subject to continual development. As a result, it takes more time to create or keep up-to-date manual tests than it does to develop test cases automatically. Also, developing and creating automated tests through traditional means typically involves using some type of rule-based approach to extract data and/or rely on only one type of isolated natural language processing technique. In this article, we have developed a new type of intelligent system that can automatically create and re-create testing artifacts by bringing together multiple sources of information (e.g., text, images, etc.), using RAG, machine learning models, and hybrid impact analysis mechanisms. The components within this intelligent system utilize techniques such as semantic role labelling, entity extraction, and vector retrieving to process requirements expressed through different forms of text, various documents, and images. Finally, large language models are being used to automatically create structured test case scenarios from the results of using the RAG methodology and producing the testing artifacts mentioned above. The proposal for a new hybrid impact scoring model is based on calculating how many different types of impacts can occur (full, partial and integrated) through examining the similarity of records (based on embedding), the relevance of clusters (based on historical edits), and other assessment tools. The new model allows for focusing on regenerating only those test cases that were impacted by the change (from the previous release) through empirical validation of results, which clearly show the following advantages over traditional methods: improved accuracy of testing, increased confidence in detecting the impact of a change, decreased manual work effort to identify impacted test cases, and so on. Therefore, the proposed method provides a flexible, adaptable, and scalable solution for maintaining high-quality test suites in a continuously changing software development environment.

title: Visiorag: A Multimodal Framework for Enhancing Recommendation System Using Vision Transformers and Rag
abstract: In the rapidly advancing field of visual search technology, traditional methods relying solely on visual features often struggle with accuracy and relevance, especially in ecommerce, where precise recommendations are crucial. Issues like keyword stuffing in product descriptions further compound these challenges. To overcome these limitations, we present VisioRAG, a multimodal recommendation framework that integrates visual and textual features. By utilizing Vision Transformers (ViT) for input query categorization and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with large language models (LLMs) for image captioning and query enhancement, VisioRAG converts image queries into contextual word embeddings. These embeddings, along with the original image queries, form the multimodal input to the framework. The system leverages Florence-2-large for image captioning, BERT for contextual embedding generation, and Google's Gemini for caption enhancement via prompt engineering. An early fusion technique effectively merges visual and textual vectors. Recommendations are made using cosine similarity, ensuring product matches that align with user intent and preferences. Our evaluation using Amazon product data across five categories shows that the fusion approach with RAG achieves the highest precision ($0.9333 \pm 0.1294$), surpassing other methods. This demonstrates VisioRAG's potential to improve product recommendations and customer satisfaction by leveraging generative AI for human-like text generation.

title: Generative AI for Musculoskeletal Medicine: A Multimodal RAG Framework for Knowledge Retrieval and Reasoning
abstract: The domain of musculoskeletal healthcare poses distinctive challenges for automated clinical support systems, given the complexity of anatomical knowledge, the necessity for image-text alignment, and the requirement for domain-specific reasoning. In this study, we present a Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) framework that is designed to retrieve and synthesise specialised medical knowledge from images in medical atlases. A local database containing domain-specific PDF content both textual and visual is integrated into our system, and a multimodal RAG pipeline is employed to generate context-aware responses for healthcare professionals. The system offers enhanced decision support, improved diagnostic reasoning, and interactive educational capabilities by aligning user queries with semantically relevant passages and illustrations. Compared to traditional LLM-based or unimodal RAG systems, our approach achieves more relevant, factually accurate, and domain-aligned responses. Experimental evaluations demonstrate its effectiveness in musculoskeletal health scenarios across metrics such as retrieval precision, multimodal consistency, and user satisfaction. This study highlights the potential of domain-specific MM-RAG architectures to transform medical information systems by combining static reference data with dynamic, intelligent assistance.

title: Self-Knowledge Retrieval Augmented Generation Framework for Patent Matching
abstract: Patent retrieval and matching based on large language models (LLMs) play a vital role in intellectual property protection. However, due to the complex structure of patent documents, dense technical terminology, and multi-modal information, traditional methods struggle to accurately identify subtle differences between patents. Existing LLM-based patent matching approaches typically rely on domain-specific pretrained or instruction tuning, which often entail high manual labeling costs and catastrophic forgetting. While retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods introduce external knowledge they fail to fully leverage LLM's capability to automatically parse patents and mine deep semantic relationships. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a self-knowledge RAG framework that guides LLMs to autonomously extract key technical entities and construct hierarchical ontological structures from patent matching queries, thereby enabling query expansion and precise retrieval. The method integrates the FAISS retrieval with a generative matching mechanism, leveraging self-knowledge to enhance the model's understanding of patent innovations and significantly improve retrieval and matching accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding performance of the proposed method on real-world patent datasets, validating its effectiveness and application potential.

title: Towards Developing a Multimodal Chat Assistant for University Stakeholders: RAG-Based Approach
abstract: University stakeholders often face difficulties in accessing timely and reliable information, especially in developing countries, where there are very few intelligent support systems. Existing rule-based chatbots are unable to handle complex, domain-specific queries and are not well-equipped to adapt to evolving institutional policies. As a fill-in-the-gap solution, we present the multimodal university chatbot with retrieval-augmented generation. The system combines the large language model with semantic retrieval to produce context-based responses from institution-centric resources, such as the university handbook. The system accepts text and image queries through the vision-language model and applies quantized inference for rapid deployment on constrained hardware. A scalable backend built with FastAPI, adjoined with a responsive frontend developed with Next.js, ensures real-time usability. Our multimodal evaluation demonstrates that the system maintains strong satisfaction scores across both text and image queries, despite increased response time for visual inputs. Furthermore, quantitative evaluation shows that hallucination is reduced from 31.7% to 6.6% in our proposed RAG-based system, confirming the effectiveness of retrieval grounding.

title: ViTCM-LLM: A Multimodal RAG Framework for Advanced TCM Clinical Decision Support
abstract: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis, particularly methods like tongue diagnosis, faces significant challenges in subjectivity and scalability. The application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to fundamental TCM tasks, such as syndrome differentiation and prescription generation, is significantly hampered by the difficulty of integrating visual tongue data with clinical text, and by the scarcity of suitable public datasets. To overcome these barriers, we introduce ViTCM-LLM, a novel framework that emulates an expert's diagnostic process by integrating multimodal language modeling with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Employing a dual-component architecture, ViTCM-LLM integrates a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL model for visual analysis with a Qwen3-based RAG for clinical reasoning. The framework was developed and validated using MedTCM, a new large-scale multimodal dataset that we introduce specifically for advanced TCM research. To properly evaluate our framework's clinical accuracy, which existing metrics fail to capture, we also developed TDEU, a domain-specific evaluation metric. Evaluated using this metric alongside standard benchmarks, our comprehensive experiments on MedTCM demonstrate that ViTCM-LLM significantly outperforms leading models, including GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash. These findings not only establish the feasibility of a generalizable tongue diagnosis model but also validate the critical role of integrating visual data for advanced TCM diagnostics. The code and data can be found at https://github.com/jw-chae/ViTCM_LLM.

These findings not only establish the feasibility of a generalizable tongue diagnosis model but also validate the critical role of integrating visual data for advanced TCM diagnostics. title: LearnRAG: Implementing Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adaptive Learning Systems
abstract: The rapid advancements in large language models have revolutionized natural language processing, yet their static knowledge bases limit their applicability in dynamic, domain-specific, and personalized contexts. Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems address this challenge by integrating retrieval mechanisms with generative models to deliver real-time, contextually enriched responses. This paper implements LearnRAG, an open-source RAG framework for personalized learning that is modular in architecture, hybrid in retrieval, and fine-tuned for generation to produce adaptive educational content. A holistic case study of LearnRAG showed scalability, efficiency, increasing learner engagement, and reducing educators' workload. Issues such as multimodal integration, content accuracy, and learning styles are discussed, and strategies for ethical deployment are developed. LearnRAG offers a robust, scalable, and adaptive platform to meet the evolving needs of learners and educators worldwide, representing a paradigm shift in GenAI-driven education.

title: A Comprehensive Review on Offline Multimodal RAG for Unified Semantic Retrieval for Documents, Images, and Audio
abstract: We have a lot of data from companies and people like documents and pictures and audio recordings. This has made it really important to have systems that can look at all these types of data and make sense of them together. Now most systems that do this are focused on text and they usually need to use services that are based in the cloud. This is a problem when we need to keep information private or when we do not have a lot of bandwidth. We need systems like retrieval augmented generation systems that can search and reason across all these types of data in a unified way. Retrieval-augmented generation systems are very useful. We should use retrieval augmented generation systems to make things easier, for us. This work is about Offline Multimodal RAG systems. Offline Multimodal RAG systems are a way to search for things in a collection of documents, images and audio. It does this by putting all these things one space where they can be easily found. The people who did this work looked at a bunch of research articles about searching for things, in many different ways learning what things mean and finding ways to make searching faster. They wanted to see how well these different ways of searching worked. They looked at things like how accurate the search results were, how long it took to get them, how much memory it used, how well it worked even when some of the information wasn't good, and how well it kept private things private. They looked at all of these things to see what worked well with Offline Multimodal RAG systems. We also summarize the most common backbone models, embedding strategies, and indexing techniques. We also point out some of the biggest problems that still need to be solved in multimodal alignment, evaluation protocols, and edge deployment. The results of this review seek to direct researchers and practitioners in the creation of secure, precise, and entirely offline multimodal RAG systems for applications involving sensitive data.

title: NextRAG: A Bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Financial Question-Answering
abstract: Financial institutions and regulators produce large volumes of complex, multilingual documents, making access to critical financial information challenging. Limited financial literacy further exacerbates this issue in countries like Bangladesh. This study introduces NextRAG, a bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for financial knowledge retrieval and question answering in the Bangladeshi context. Unlike conventional RAG pipelines, NextRAG employs specialized preprocessing for noisy financial PDFs using OCR. The framework integrates sparse retrieval with BM25, probabilistic query modeling via Dirichlet smoothing, and fuses results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), followed by cross-encoder re-ranking. It also supports Bangla and English interactions through languageaware prompting. Evaluation on a diverse bilingual financial Q&A dataset shows that NextRAG consistently outperforms conventional RAG, achieving a mean cosine similarity of 0.77 and an F1 score of 68.3%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of hybrid retrieval in handling complex financial terminology, reducing retrieval errors and hallucinations in a low-resource bilingual setting.

title: Fine-Tuning MedGemma for Clinical Captioning to Enhance Multimodal RAG over Malaysia CPGs
abstract: General Vision-Language Models inadequately generate clinically-precise captions required for high-stakes medical applications, constraining Retrieval-Augmented Generation effectiveness when querying Malaysian Clinical Practice Guidelines with images. We introduce a specialization framework that adapts MedGemma into a high-quality query generator. Knowledge distillation addresses annotation limitations, synthesizing training corpora across dermatological, fundoscopic, and radiographic domains. QLORA facilitates efficient model fine-tuning. Complementary evaluation strategies validate our approach which includes classification analysis that reveals marked performance gains, and novel RAGAS framework application to caption assessment demonstrates substantial faithfulness and correctness improvements. This research establishes a robust medical VLM specialization methodology, creating a factually-grounded query generation component critical for multimodal clinical decision support systems.

title: An Agentic, Multimodal RAG Framework for Risk-Aware Surgical Robotics User Manual Creation
abstract: In the medical device domain, the user manual is a safety-critical and foundational artifact that directly impacts clinical outcomes. For complex surgical robotic systems, inaccurate manuals increase procedural risks. Despite their importance, traditional user manual creation is labor-intensive, error-prone, and typically deferred until late in development, limiting early validation and increasing project risk. This paper presents an AI-driven framework for accelerated, risk-aware user manual creation using agentic AI and video-based content ingestion. The proposed system combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with autonomous AI agents to continuously draft, review, and refine manual content throughout the product lifecycle. By integrating surgical workflow videos with design and regulatory documentation, the framework enables richer contextual understanding and more precise procedural guidance. Practical insights from real-world surgical robotics development demonstrate how early, automated documentation can reduce human error, accelerate development timelines, and strengthen clinical safety, transforming user manuals from a compliance requirement into a proactive risk-mitigation tool. The paper will present: 1) Introduction: motivation, problem statement and our objective, 2) Regulatory and clinical context, 3) Technical architecture of the AI-driven system, 4) Methods for video-based content ingestion and semantic reasoning, 5) Implementation results and lessons learned from real-world surgical robotics development, and 6) Conclusion and future work.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generative AI for Adaptive Data Engineering in Healthcare Systems
abstract: The sudden explosion of healthcare information, Electronic Health Records (EHRs) to medical images and sensor streams, has led to a desperate requirement of intelligent systems and systems that can be used to efficiently gather and process information, and provide context-driven information. The new method presented in this paper, which is called RetrievalAugmented Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Adaptive Data Engineering (RAG-ADE) is aimed at supporting the process of data integration and prediction in healthcare. The model architecture is retrieval-based embedding based on generative transformer backbone to enable to correctly and explainably process information in clinical workflow. The RAG-ADE is made up of three key stages: retrieval, adaptive data engineering and generative reasoning. The retrieval stage of the system extracts medical data in both structured and unstructured forms, and the adaptive engineering part normalizes multimodal medical data. The generative layer represents a consistent diagnostic perspective and prediction using the assistance of attention mechanisms by transformers. The experimental findings on multimodal data on Kaggle and comparisons against state-of-the-art models such as MedGPT and Health-BERT demonstrate that RAG-ADE has an accuracy of 95.3 %, precision of 94.5 % and recall of 94.8 % and outperform the baseline architectures. The proposed model has low computational latency and higher data consistency, which makes it suitable in clinical decision support systems in real-time. The RAG-ADE model fills a gap between the problem of databased inference and human-like reasoning within healthcare analytics by connecting retrieval intelligence with generative adaptability. This paper offers a solution that is scalable and interpretable to enable further development of AI-based healthcare diagnostics and adaptive data engineering within a clinical setting.

title: DeepSem: Multilayer Semantic Image Retrieval for High-Accuracy Multimodal RAG in Industrial Applications
abstract: The technical service costs associated with industrial software represent a significant portion of its lifecycle expenditures. For instance, large-scale software systems, such as SAP ERP, often require hundreds of maintenance engineers to provide troubleshooting services for thousands of users. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a potential technique to perform as robot consultants, substantially reducing human resource costs in customer service. To achieve human-level response accuracy, the prevailing strategy involves implementing Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) frameworks which equip MLLMs with detailed information and contextual references. However, existing MRAG frameworks are not well equipped to handle image data, such as user-provided error screenshots. Therefore, retrieval accuracy remains a critical bottleneck. This paper proposes an innovative retrieval methodology based on our multilayer semantic model, termed DeepSem, which deconstructs one image into three hierarchical semantic layers. During retrieval, each layer is independently matched, scored through weighted evaluation, and aggregated to enhance the output quality of large models. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an improved retrieval accuracy of 43. 9% and 30. 6% over MLLM baseline and naïve multimodal RAG frameworks, respectively, without significant increases in computational latency. Finally, we highlight the broad applicability of this multilayer semantic multimodal RAG approach, offering advanced technical solutions for generalized customer service and intelligent QA systems in other industrial scenarios.

title: An Intelligent TCM Diagnosis System with Localized LLMs and Modular Multimodal Reasoning Enhanced by RAG
abstract: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis relies on multimodal data including tongue images, voice signals, pulse waveforms, and symptom descriptions obtained through inspection, auscultation, inquiry, and palpation. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and multimodal integration offer new opportunities for intelligent TCM diagnostics. However, current approaches suffer from unstructured modality handling, inefficient cross-modal fusion, and limited interpretability, hindering clinical adoption. This paper proposes a locally deployed LLM-based TCM diagnostic system with structured multimodal perception. Four AI agents—Observation, Listening, Inquiry, and Palpation—are coordinated via Modular Component Processing (MCP) and multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (mRAG) for structured feature extraction and semantic fusion. A central reasoning module generates diagnostic results and personalized health advice using structured prompts and patient history. A certainty assessment mechanism further enhances interpretability and reliability. Experiments demonstrate strong generalizability and scalability, validating the system’s potential for intelligent multimodal TCM diagnosis.

title: Instruct-Imagen: Image Generation with Multi-modal Instruction
abstract: This paper presents Instruct-Imagen, a model that tackles heterogeneous image generation tasks and generalizes across unseen tasks. We introduce multi-modal in-struction for image generation, a task representation artic-ulating a range of generation intents with precision. It uses natural language to amalgamate disparate modalities (e.g., text, edge, style, subject, etc.), such that abundant generation intents can be standardized in a uniform format. We then build Instruct - Imagen by fine-tuning a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model with two stages. First, we adapt the model using the retrieval-augmented training, to enhance model's capabilities to ground its generation on external multi-modal context. Subsequently, we fine-tune the adapted model on diverse image generation tasks that requires vision-language understanding (e.g., subject-driven generation, etc.), each paired with a multi-modal instruction encapsulating the task's essence. Human evaluation on various image generation datasets re-veals that Instruct-Imagen matches or surpasses prior task-specific models in-domain and demonstrates promising generalization to unseen and more complex tasks. Our evaluation suite will be made publicly available.

title: LLM-Driven Multimodal Knowledge Graph Construction for Industrial Process With Prompt Optimization and Fuzzy RAG
abstract: The industrial flotation process involves multimodal data and cross-procedural knowledge, presenting significant challenges for knowledge system management and traditional knowledge graph (KG) construction methods. This study develops a large language model (LLM)-driven framework to construct a domain-specific multimodal KG. The Flotation Knowledge Tree ontology is designed as the structural backbone of the KG to organize multi-level operations and interactions while integrating heterogeneous flotation data. To enhance the LLM's domain adaptability, adaptive prompt optimization is proposed to iteratively refine the extraction template with flotation-specific examples and performance feedback, enabling more accurate triple extraction. Additionally, a fuzzy information entropy-driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) method is proposed, leveraging fuzzy logic to assign weights to key terms and numerical contexts to preserve causal relationships and semantic integrity under data uncertainty. Furthermore, we established a two-stage LLM-driven pipeline to generate initial triples using a LoRA fine-tuned lightweight LLM with the optimized prompt and fuzzy RAG context, followed by refinement with a large-scale LLM for precision and ontology alignment. Validated triples are mapped onto the Flotation Knowledge Tree to form a structured, high-quality KG with minimal manual intervention. This framework fuses ontology structuring, fuzzy semantic retrieval, and LLM reasoning to enable automated, domain-tailored knowledge assembly for industrial flotation processes. The constructed KG is evaluated using the Flotation Knowledge Tree-based method, achieving a score of 0.92, with a structural score of 0.97 and a semantic score of 0.88, demonstrating robustness and coherence.
